title: 3 aspirations for this school year
author: Fred Ende
summary: Fred Ende, director of curriculum and instructional services at Putnam/Northern Westchester BOCES, sets out three aspirations to guide his leadership in the 2026-2027 school year. The first is to study competency-based education deeply as New York moves its graduation requirements away from assessments and credits toward competencies, a model he notes has never been fully implemented. The second is to keep embracing change and helping others navigate it, drawing on a year of professional and personal shifts. The third, framed through Voltaire's warning about perfection, is to act through a lens of innovation and share partially formed ideas so colleagues can rally around improving them. The piece is a short reflective model of how an education leader can name a few focused goals at the start of a year.
points: New York's shift to a fully competency-based graduation model is presented as a rare chance to make learning more authentic and engaging.
Ende treats supporting others through change as part of leadership, not only managing one's own response to it.
He argues that sharing half-formed ideas invites collaboration more readily than presenting a finished plan.
Limiting himself to three focal aspirations is itself a leadership choice, since he admits a tendency to set too many goals.
quotes: Shifting from an assessment and credit structure to one driven purely by competencies, there is a lot of opportunity for students, staff, and communities to come together to change teaching and learning for the better across New York.

In truth, a fully competency-based model has never been done before, and there is a lot for me to learn about the successes and challenges other states have had in incorporating competency-based education into their systems.
Our lives are constantly shifting, and while that is hard for us as humans, it is a necessity of life and the world we live in.

One aspiration for me in 2026-2027 is to continue embracing change and helping others navigate it. Sometimes it isn’t just about how change affects us; it can also be about how we support others as they shift in their way of being.
Voltaire’s idea that we can get mired in perfection and never actually accomplish anything is worth noting. The only way to truly achieve is to be open to making mistakes along the way.
People love to come together to work around something, at times even more so than when a plan is already fully fleshed out.
These three, though, are areas where I want to strongly focus as the year begins, and where I think I can have the most impact on those in my professional and personal circles.
